title: Noon Raccoon Rooftop Run
brief: Original 8-bit first-level platform-game instrumental, about 90 seconds, with a seamless loop: two pulse voices, stepped triangle bass, clocked noise drums, a bright immediate hook, fast chord arpeggios, a contrasting key section, then a return to the opening.

sections.intent: Bright G-major route: state a short, leaping hook over a rising pulse arpeggio.
A lower E-minor detour with a tighter contour and a B7 pull back toward E.
Return to G major and the opening hook's register; stronger lead and backbeat accents carry the high point.

decisions: style:form: The level is a route to explore, so borrow game/overworld's forward-moving form for the A–B–A loop while keeping the pulse-channel language primary.
tempo: 128 BPM is this piece's choice; 48 bars of 4/4 make the loop exactly 90 seconds.

melody_durations:pulse_lead: Shortened the turnaround eighth to a sixteenth on the second bar of each four-bar phrase; the extra duration gives the short hook one quick articulation while retaining its readable eighth-note core.
vertical: Restored the return to the opening melody register; this removes the nine B4/C6 minor-ninth clashes while keeping the return higher than the lower E-minor detour.

outside_chord.melody: Changed the second phrase cycle so its strong-position non-chord tones move to the following chord tone before the leap; the return now uses the original G-major hook instead of a third-transposed line that created new unresolved tones.

parallels: Inverted the recurring downbeat bass notes to chord thirds at bars 5, 9, 13, 17, 37, 41 and 45; those landings preserve the harmony while breaking parallel-fifth motion with the lead in both G-major statements and at the E-minor turn.
stiffness:pulse_arp: Replaced held triad blocks with individual monophonic sixteenth notes in an up/down chord pattern, so the score and MIDI expose the actual moving arpeggio.

builtin_preset:pulse_lead: Keep chip_pulse12 because its 12.5 percent duty is the requested narrow pulse voice and it makes the loop render repeatably; no Surge substitute was selected without a listening comparison.

builtin_preset:pulse_arp: Use chip_pulse25 for the second pulse voice and write each arpeggio step directly; its 25 percent pulse is distinct from the lead and is repeatable without an external patch.
plan:drain_skip: Mark the detour harmony faster because review counts the section-entry change as 1.00 chord changes per bar versus 0.94 in the opening, matching the written plan to the score.

association.whole: At noon, a raccoon gives a wink from a porch and launches on a waffle barge across scrub. A leak swells into a shortcut past gnarled roots, a lemon bounces, and one tumble sends the raft by a sun-warm kiln before the runner returns to the porch.

gives.what: The porch departure, drain detour, and porch return set a 16+16+16 bar A–B–A loop.
The sunny launch and return sit in G major; the leaking shortcut shifts to E minor and uses B7 to turn home.
A compact leaping hook carries the wink; the lower, stepwise drain phrase is the tumble; the return restores the opening hook after the detour.
Sixteenth-note pulse arpeggios suggest the waffle barge's bounce; a single noise channel alternates thuds, snares and hats, with short phrase-end tumbles.
Four console-like voices only: narrow pulse melody, arpeggiated pulse chords, 16-step triangle bass and clocked noise drums.

plan.identity: A short rooftop hook stated over a written 16th-note pulse arpeggio, with a low E-minor detour and a G-major return.

high_point.means: The opening hook returns after the lower detour; its lead and noise backbeat use the strongest section velocities, without adding tracks.

sections.differs: The first statement of the rooftop route and its short hook.
The E-minor detour lowers the hook, thins the drum accents and tightens the melody contour.
The opening G-major hook returns at its original register after the lower E-minor section; the stronger lead and backbeat lift the high point.
